lines.text: Robert Boyle took a diamond to bed.
In October 1663, he borrowed a diamond from a Mr Clayton.
lines.say: In October sixteen sixty three, he borrowed a diamond from a Mister Clayton.

lines.text: Rubbed on cloth in the dark, it shone like rotten wood.
So he took it to bed to test it in the dark.
He saw it shine inside the curtains of his bed.
Pressing it with a steel bodkin also made light.
It also pulled small light things toward it.
He wrote it all up in a letter to Sir Robert Moray.
lines.say: He wrote it all up in a letter to Sir Robert Murray.

lines.text: The note was read to the Royal Society the next day.
Boyle printed his account in 1664, in a book on colors.

post.caption: Robert Boyle took a diamond to bed. In October 1663, the scientist borrowed a diamond from a Mr Clayton. Rubbed on cloth in the dark, it shone like rotten wood, so he took it to bed to test it in the dark. Pressing it with a steel bodkin also made light, and it pulled small light things toward it. He wrote it all up in a letter to Sir Robert Moray, and the note was read to the Royal Society the next day. Boyle printed his account in 1664, in a book on colors.
